title: Elon Musk on AGI, the energy bottleneck, humanoid robots and why AI-native companies win
summary: Wide-ranging 2026 conversation with Peter Diamandis. Musk argues we are in the singularity, expects AGI in 2026, says white-collar work goes first, and names electricity and cooling as the real bottleneck for AI. He also explains how cross-industry problem solving became his edge.

principles.text: Companies that are fully AI-driven will beat those that keep humans in tasks AI can do; one manual step ruins the whole spreadsheet.
principles.quote: What this means is that companies that are entirely AI will demolish companies that are not.

principles.text: Skills that are routine in one industry become a superpower when transplanted into another, so solve problems across many arenas.
principles.quote: if you apply automotive manufacturing technology to satellites and rockets. Uh it's like being Superman.

principles.text: Identify the current limiting factor; for AI today it is electricity generation and cooling, not chips.
principles.quote: Um, electricity generation is the limiting factor.

principles.text: If you cannot stop a technological wave, participate so you can steer it instead of watching from the sidelines.
principles.quote: I can either be a spectator or a participant but I can't stop it.

principles.text: Choose optimism: it gives a better quality of life even if you turn out to be wrong.
principles.quote: it is better to be a an optimist and wrong than a pessimist and right.

principles.text: Safe AI starts with honesty; forcing contradictory beliefs on a system makes it go insane.
